page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.large is a burstable instance type belonging to the ecs.t6 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned in the lower tier of compute capability. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1161.28 and 2371.48 respectively, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block cached speed of 187.49 GB/sec, which drops to a poor 22.38 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and database operations also reflect limited throughput, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 969.78 and database operations scoring 701.22, both in the bottom 10% of performance.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and low baseline network bandwidth, the ecs.t6-c1m4.large offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with low average CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes. However, the tradeoff is limited sustained performance, as evidenced by its poor multi-core Geekbench score of 1822.0 and static web serving throughput of 2.58 GB/sec. This server is best suited for lightweight applications, small-scale development or testing environments, low-traffic web servers, and basic background tasks rather than resource-intensive databases or real-time data processing.
